concepts.title: Rāmacandra and Guṇacandra and the Painful-Rasa Thesis (c. 1200 CE)
concepts.excerpt: The work is institutionally underappreciated. Only four manuscripts survive.

concepts.title: The Painful-Rasa Thesis — Jain Counter to Abhinava
concepts.excerpt: By 1200, Abhinavagupta's framework had become canonical: all rasas are essentially pleasurable; tragic, fearful, and macabre content produces pleasure-via-aesthetic-mechanism rather than pain.

concepts.title: The New Scholars' Cognitive-Error Theory of Rasa
concepts.excerpt: In Rasagaṅgādhara c. 1650, Jagannātha reports the position of certain "New Scholars" (Navyas) on the nature of rasa.

concepts.title: The Four Essential Rasas and Four Ends of Man Homology
concepts.excerpt: | Stable Emotion | Essential Rasa | End of Man | |---|---|---| | Desire (rati) | Erotic (śṛṅgāra) | Love/pleasure (kāma) | | Anger (krodha) | Violent (raudra) | Wealth (artha) | | Determination (utsāha) | Heroic (vīra) | Morality (dharma) | | Impassivity (nirveda) | Peaceful (śānta) | Liberation (mokṣa) |

concepts.title: The Four Fusion Modes — Expansion, Enlargement, Turbulence, Agitation
concepts.excerpt: Dhanika c.

concepts.title: Dhanika and the Fusion Modes (c. 975 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Dhanika was Dhanaṃjaya's brother (or near-relative; their father's name is identical).

concepts.title: Vidyānātha and the Encomium Poetics (c. 1320 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Vidyānātha wrote Pratāparudrīya — Ornament of the Fame of King Pratāparudra — at the court of Pratāparudra, king of Warangal in today's Andhra Pradesh, in the first decades of the fourteenth century.

concepts.title: Bhakti-Rasa as Twelfth Rasa — The Devotional Revolution
concepts.excerpt: The Sanskrit aesthetic tradition's nine-rasa scheme had been canonical for centuries by the time the Bengali Vaishnava revival began.

concepts.title: Jīva Gosvāmin and the Theology of Rasa (c. 1541–1550 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Jīva Gosvāmin (b. 1513 or 1523) was Rūpa Gosvāmin's nephew — the son of Rūpa's younger brother.

concepts.title: Hemādri and the Bhakti-Rasa Defense (c. 1300 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Hemādri was the chief minister of the Yadava kings of Devagiri in their last decades of autonomy before absorption into the Delhi Sultanate in 1294.

concepts.title: The Vraja-Women Defense — Married Women as Erotic Foundational Factor
concepts.excerpt: The Bengali Vaishnava devotional tradition centers its devotional erotic on Krishna's love for the gopis — the cowherd women of Vraja.

concepts.title: Kavikarṇapūra and the Divine Jewel of Ornamentation (c. 1550 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Paramānandadāsasena Kavikarṇapūra was the son of one of Chaitanya's direct disciples — Śivānandasena.

concepts.title: Vopadeva and the Pearls of the Bhāgavata (c. 1300 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Vopadeva was, before anything else, a grammarian. He was known in late thirteenth-century Maharashtra principally as the author of an elementary Sanskrit grammar that found wide circulation.

concepts.title: Arjunavarmadeva and the Elixir for the Rasika (c. 1215 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Arjunavarmadeva was a king who described himself as "lamp to the family of Bhoja" — a descendant in the political and intellectual lineage of the great Paramāra ruler-aesthetician of Dhārā who had written Light on Passion two centuries earlier.

concepts.title: Bhānudatta and the River of Rasa (c. 1500 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Bhānudatta was a northeastern Brahman poet who worked at a southwestern Islamicate court around 1500 CE.

concepts.title: Bhakti Aesthetic Collapse — Devotee as Actor/Character
concepts.excerpt: This concept files to cross-domain because the Bengali Vaishnava devotional aesthetics of Rūpa and Jīva Gosvāmin cannot be understood without holding eastern-spirituality bhakti theology AND creative-practice performance theory simultaneously.

concepts.title: Jagannātha and the Vedānticization of Rasa (c. 1650 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Jagannātha Paṇḍitarāja (c. 1620-1665) was a Telangana Brahman who passed his youth "under the care of the emperor of Delhi," Shāh Jahān.

concepts.title: Viśvanātha and the Mirror of Literary Art (c. 1350 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Viśvanātha hailed from a family of poet-intellectuals serving the royal house of Kalinga (today's Odisha) — same family region as Vidyādhara, the earlier poet-theorist whose work Viśvanātha apparently never engaged.

concepts.title: Viśvanāthadeva and the Vedānta Bridge (1592 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Viśvanāthadeva is virtually unknown to Indian intellectual history. His principal work — Sāhityasudhāsindhu (Nectar Ocean of Literary Art) — was not edited and published until 1978.

concepts.title: Vedānta-Rasa — The Bliss Component Revealed
concepts.excerpt: For 1,200 years, the rasa tradition had grounded its framework variously in Mīmāṃsā ritual-theory (Bhaṭṭa Nāyaka), Kashmir Shaiva consciousness-theory (Abhinavagupta), Sāṃkhya-yoga mental-state typology (Dhanika), and Buddhist logical apparatus (Mahima Bhaṭṭa).

concepts.title: Anantadāsa as Commentator on Viśvanātha (c. 1400 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Anantadāsa is almost certainly Viśvanātha's son.

concepts.title: Lokanātha Chakravartin and the Secular Collapse (c. 1690 CE)
concepts.excerpt: The commentary was published as anonymous by its first editor; De 1988 attributed it to Lokanātha without providing direct evidence, since a commentator of that name also wrote on the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa.

concepts.title: Bhaṭṭa Toṭa and the Imitation Critique (c. 975 CE)
concepts.excerpt: We know Bhaṭṭa Toṭa (sometimes Tauta) primarily through what his student wrote.

concepts.title: Dhanaṃjaya and the Ten Dramatic Forms (c. 975 CE)
concepts.excerpt: Dhanaṃjaya was a courtier of King Vākpati Munja of the Paramāra dynasty, who ruled the central Indian city of Dhārā from approximately 974/975 to 994/995.
